guide.title: Is refacing right for your kitchen?
guide.intro: Also known as cabinet refacing, this approach changes the appearance of your kitchen without replacing every cabinet. Here is what to consider.

items.title: Cabinet boxes worth keeping
items.text: We assess the condition of the cabinet boxes and the existing layout. If their structure suits the project, they can form the basis of the transformation.

items.title: Doors, fronts and details
items.text: We work with you to select new doors, drawer fronts, finishes and hardware. The assessment identifies which elements to keep and which to replace.

items.title: What determines the price
items.text: The number of doors and drawers, materials, hardware and requested changes affect the cost. Assessing your kitchen allows us to prepare an estimate for your project.

items.title: Refacing or a new kitchen?
items.text: Do you like your current kitchen layout? Refacing may be an option. If you want to change the layout completely or the cabinet boxes are damaged, a new kitchen may be more suitable.

items.title: Wood, melamine or thermofoil
items.text: Tell us your cabinet material and its condition when you contact us. We assess the possibilities rather than recommending the same treatment for every kitchen.

items.title: Let’s discuss your project
items.text: Based in the Laurentians, we take on projects according to their scope and location. Tell us about yours.
